If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1.0–1.5% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect momentum reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 7+ days, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% in late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 7+ days, increase forecast by 0.3–0.7% in late horizon (16–30 days) to counteract prolonged bearish pressure.  
If sentiment is neutral or mixed over 5+ days, apply no correction unless forecast deviates >1.5% from recent 7-day average — then adjust by ±0.5% to align with mean reversion.
